method: Read the supplied fresh own-Native sample and producer summary. Bound current sample, summary, catalog, selection, compressed immutable source table, producer and permitted language guidance by actual SHA-256 and byte counts. No regeneration or runtime evaluation was performed.

Directly inspected all 414 supplied English/Native record pairs, typed parameters and every explicit member owner/context in manageable batches. Review included all 192 high-risk selectors, 36 required-distinction/protocol selectors and all 186 added exact overrides. No other Native catalog or locale glossary was used as translation guidance.

Used only canonical English, glossaries/en.json, glossaries/de.json and editorial-policy.json for language/terminology guidance. Compared negation, conditions, source attribution, time, actors, trust direction, authentication/authorization/admission, custody/validation, signing/encryption, transport/DNSSEC, Credential Guard/token filtering, DNSSEC verdicts, JWT invalid/unknown/unsupported, NTLM fallback and occurrence-bound PAM controls.

For role ambiguity, used actual operationKind/actor/owner and current named canonical producer excerpts, not a literal shared English action verb or step-ID substring. Current module hashes were compared to historical language-independent operation-role evidence; historical sourceSet acceptance was not restamped. Current labWire/Kubernetes event producers do copy shared details onto both send and receive.

Consulted current publication constructors and provider-switch call, client candidate versus validator SessionBaseKey producers, borrowed FAST ticket send/receive, SSH copy/account/transport-proof failure, Mac volume ownership and Linux recorded audit decision producers. Concrete defects were decided from current source actions, not merely differences from English.

Saved source excerpts/hashes and batch-specific analysis privately. All report member verdicts are direct reviewer dispositions; iteration/JSON serialization only assembled the ledger and did not generate translation-quality verdicts or fabricate model calls.

conclusions: Send/receive overrides are legitimate when they describe the actual member action rather than the shared exchange caption.
Client-local candidate SessionBaseKey is not a validator return and proves no successful account validation.
publishAnswer from/to dnsProviderB is a provider publication event, not receipt by a resolver using cached keys.

SSH copied certificate mismatch is failed authentication after copying, not failed copy. The wrong-transport signature branch is also authentication failure, not session-channel establishment failure.
Independently provisioned volume ownership is not mere object possession. The Linux audit object records an access decision rather than performing a new audit inspection.

findings.title: Publication stage is incorrectly described as resolver receipt
findings.rationale: Both exact owners are the payload/summary of publishAnswer, not the later resolver response. Current src/dnssec-signing-cases.js:399 calls publishAnswer with from=to=dnsProviderB. The constructor at 111-114 updates the published provider generation and calls a.publish; dnssec-authoring.js:139-149 makes a publication event to the provider publication store. The resolver cache context is a separate observe at line 400 and the later finishLookup follows it. The German empfangen and attached cached-key receipt qualification move this action across the publication/receipt boundary. The odd receive-b-answer step identifier is not authority to contradict its actual current producer. The other publication captions (230,257,341,414) correctly say veröffentlichen and are not findings.

findings.title: Wrong-transport authentication proof is labeled session setup failure
findings.rationale: The session variant is a signature over transport-0 used in transport-1. Current ssh-access-lab.js:408-416 rejects that possession proof with signature_wrong_transport, sets sessions.ssh.authenticated=false, and sends SSH authentication failure; no session channel is opened (the channel branch is 417-418). Sitzungseinrichtung falsely relocates the failed event to session establishment and drops the authentication failure nature. The word session in the stable field ID is not a session-creation operation. This is a new exact Source13 finding, not a reopening of any historical finding.
